key_highlights: ASX shed $90bn in a week as rate-rise fears and oil price surge pressured miners and banks (Headlines 49, 73)
AUD weakened sharply on growth scare, compounding pressure on import-dependent sectors (Headline 59)
Iron ore 'bloodletting' underway, pressuring BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX valuations (Headline 55)
RBA flagged rental inflation as a key concern, raising probability of further rate hikes (Headline 71)
Oil prices surged as suppression efforts failed; fuel prices to rise 30c, hitting consumer margins (Headlines 60, 47)
ANZ.AX post-3,500-job-cut strategy still faces execution risk (Headline 38)
Housing market correction deepens: no spring bounce at auctions, prices crashing, first-home buyers surging (Headlines 37, 62)
Nvidia's 2GW Australia AI data-centre push signals long-term tech infrastructure tailwind (Headline 16)
Australia softened local gas supply rules, easing Asian energy-security fears (Headline 74)
Mining cap-raising wave led by Canaccord signals capital stress in junior resources (Headline 50)

sectors.trend: Sharp deterioration. Iron ore 'bloodletting' underway; oil surge benefits energy names but weighs on industrial metals. Junior miners scrambling for cap raises. Gold underperforming ('gold schmould').
sectors.implications: BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX face margin compression on iron ore. Gold miners (GOLD.AX, NVG.AX) lack a safe-haven bid. Small caps (PolarX, Sunstone, Manuka) volatile. Canaccord-led cap raises dilute equity holders.

sectors.trend: Banks under pressure from rising bond yields compressing NIMs and rate-rise fears hitting equity valuations. ANZ.AX post-restructuring still executing. Superannuation reform debate adds policy uncertainty.
sectors.implications: CBA.AX, NAB.AX, ANZ.AX, WBC.AX face headwinds from yield curve steepening and credit-risk concerns. Super fund flows may shift amid reform debate. Defensive dividend appeal intact but capped.

sectors.trend: Oil price surge benefits producers; Australia's softened gas supply rules support Santos.AX and energy security narrative. Fuel price rise of 30c pressures downstream and transport.
sectors.implications: Santos.AX, Woodside.AX benefit from gas policy easing. BHP.AX energy division supported by oil. Downstream (Ampol) and transport (Qantas.AX) face cost pressure.

sectors.trend: Woolworths.AX price-freeze credibility hit; fuel and import costs rising. Housing correction boosting first-home buyer activity but overall consumer confidence weak.
sectors.implications: WES.AX, WOW.AX face margin pressure from input costs. REITs (GPG.AX, SPG.AX) pressured by rental inflation and falling property values. Flight cancellations hit Qantas.AX.

sectors.trend: Nvidia 2GW Australia AI push signals structural demand for data-centre infrastructure. AI monitoring (Datadog, Dynatrace) and agentic AI themes active globally.
sectors.implications: ASX-listed data-centre and power names (e.g., VIX.AX, IAG.AX) benefit. Long-term tailwind for Australian tech infrastructure despite near-term market stress.

sectors.trend: NDIS funding cuts and superannuation reform debate create policy uncertainty. Global pharma (Novo Nordisk, BioMarin) active but limited ASX direct impact.
sectors.implications: CSL.AX, SGH.AX, WES.AX (health) face mixed signals. NDIS cuts may pressure allied-health providers.

AUD weakness amplifying import-cost inflation and consumer squeeze
Housing correction accelerating with policy implications for REITs and banks

Superannuation reform debate creating policy uncertainty for financials

risk_assessment.risk_factor: RBA rate hike / bond yield spike
risk_assessment.mitigation: Reduce duration exposure; favour short-duration and floating-rate instruments; hedge with gold and energy hedges
Underweight BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX; rotate into oil/gold exposure; monitor Chinese stimulus signals
Favour domestic-revenue companies; avoid import-heavy consumer names; consider AUD-hedged commodity exposure

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Housing market correction spilling into credit losses
risk_assessment.mitigation: Monitor bank NPL data; underweight high-LVR REITs; favour defensive dividend payers
Maintain energy and gold hedges; monitor freight cost pass-through to consumer staples

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Mining sector dilution via cap raises
risk_assessment.mitigation: Avoid junior miners with imminent raises; favour cash-flow-positive majors

opportunities.recommendation: Overweight energy producers on oil surge and gas policy easing
opportunities.rationale: Oil price spike plus Australia's softened gas supply rules create a favourable backdrop for domestic energy names

opportunities.recommendation: Position for AI infrastructure build-out in Australia
opportunities.rationale: Nvidia's 2GW Australia push signals multi-year capex cycle benefiting power, data-centre, and construction names

opportunities.recommendation: Selective gold exposure on geopolitical risk
opportunities.rationale: Middle East escalation and AUD weakness support gold despite near-term 'schmould'; quality producers preferred

defensive_moves.recommendation: Reduce iron ore and industrial metals exposure
defensive_moves.rationale: Iron ore 'bloodletting' underway; no clear floor visible; cap-raise dilution risk in juniors

defensive_moves.recommendation: Trim high-yield REITs and rate-sensitive financials
defensive_moves.rationale: Rising bond yields compress valuations; housing correction raises credit-risk concerns for banks

defensive_moves.recommendation: Increase cash and short-duration bond allocation
defensive_moves.rationale: Market volatility elevated; $90bn ASX drawdown signals further downside risk; preserve capital

market_outlook.short_term: Bearish. ASX likely to extend the $90bn weekly drawdown as rate-rise fears, oil-driven inflation, and iron ore weakness persist. RBA rental-inflation commentary keeps hawkish bias. AUD weakness adds import-cost pressure. Expect continued volatility in miners and banks. 1–3 month range: further 5–8% downside risk on ^AXJO.
market_outlook.long_term: Cautiously constructive on a 6–12 month horizon if RBA pauses and iron ore stabilises. AI infrastructure capex (Nvidia 2GW), gas policy reform, and housing correction creating first-home buyer demand offer structural positives. Superannuation reform debate could be a tailwind for financials if resolved constructively. Key risk: prolonged commodity downturn or geopolitical escalation.
